questions.title: Question 1: What a package is (8 marks)
questions.prompt: Define a package, state two advantages and the two categories, and give an example of each category. (8 marks)

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: A package is a group of related classes organised into a folder, which might have sub-folders. (2 marks)

steps.title: Advantages
steps.body: It promotes writing better and more maintainable code, and it prevents the possibility of name conflicts. (2 marks)

steps.title: Categories
steps.body: Built-in packages come bundled with the language (the Java API), for example `java.util`, which holds `Scanner`. User-defined packages must be created by programmers, for example `pkg` with classes `A` and `B`. (4 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** A group of related classes in a folder; maintainable code and no name conflicts; built-in and user-defined.

questions.title: Question 2: Imports (8 marks)
questions.prompt: A program uses `Scanner`, `ArrayList`, `PrintWriter`, `String` and `Math`. State the imports it needs and why. Then say what `javac` reports for `Date` when `java.util.*` and `java.sql.*` are both imported, and the repair. (8 marks)

steps.title: The imports
steps.body: `import java.util.Scanner;` and `import java.util.ArrayList;` (or `java.util.*`), and `import java.io.PrintWriter;` (or `java.io.*`). `String` and `Math` are in `java.lang`, which is imported by default. (4 marks)

steps.title: The conflict
steps.body: `error: reference to Date is ambiguous` (both `java.util.Date` and `java.sql.Date` match). Import only the class you need, or write the full name, `java.util.Date`. (4 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** Three imports; `String` and `Math` need none; the ambiguity is repaired with one import or a full name.

creating-and-using.title: Creating, compiling and using a package

questions.title: Question 3: Build a package (12 marks)
questions.prompt: Create a package `greetings` with a class `Greeting` that has a method `hello(String name)`, and a tester that uses it. Give the folder layout, the first lines of the source files, and the commands to compile and run, and say where the class files end up. (12 marks)

steps.title: Layout
steps.body: `src/greetings/Greeting.java`, `src/GreetingTester.java` and a `classes` folder. The folder under `src` is named like the package. (3 marks)

steps.title: Sources
steps.body: `Greeting.java` starts with `package greetings;` and declares `public class Greeting`. The tester starts with `import greetings.Greeting;`. (3 marks)

steps.title: Commands
steps.body: From the folder above `src` and `classes`: `javac -d classes -sourcepath src src/greetings/Greeting.java`, then `javac -d classes -classpath classes src/GreetingTester.java`, then `java -classpath classes GreetingTester`. (4 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** The tester prints `Hello, Kago`; the class files are in `classes`.

questions.title: Question 4: Diagnose (12 marks)
questions.prompt: Explain each failure and give the repair: (a) the tester is compiled with `javac -d out src/pkgTester.java` and reports `package pkg does not exist`; (b) `java pkgTester` reports `Could not find or load main class`; (c) `Account.java` with `package bankAccounts;` is saved in `src` and the tester reports `package bankAccounts does not exist`. (12 marks)

steps.title: Part (a)
steps.body: The compiler searches only the current folder for `pkg`. Repair: `javac -d classes -classpath classes src/pkgTester.java`, after the package has been compiled into `classes`. (4 marks)

steps.title: Part (b)
steps.body: The launcher also searches only the current folder, and `pkgTester.class` is in `classes`. Repair: from the folder above `classes`, `java -classpath classes pkgTester`. (4 marks)

steps.title: Part (c)
steps.body: With `-sourcepath src` the compiler looks for `src/bankAccounts/Account.java`; the folder must be named like the package. Repair: move the file to `src/bankAccounts` and compile again. (4 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** Give the class path to javac, give it to java, and name the folder after the package.

questions.title: Question 5: public, protected and default (8 marks)
questions.prompt: A class `Item` has no modifier in the package `shop`, and `Till` has a public method `open()` and a method `key()` with no modifier. A tester in the default package uses them. In another package `base`, `Animal` has a protected method `sound()`. State what `javac` reports for each use and why. (8 marks)

steps.title: Default access
steps.body: `Item is not public in shop; cannot be accessed from outside package` and `key() is not public in Till; cannot be accessed from outside package`: with no modifier a class or member is visible only within its package. `open()` is public and compiles. (4 marks)

steps.title: Protected access
steps.body: A sub class in another package may call the protected `sound()`; a class that is neither in the package nor a sub class gets `sound() has protected access in Animal`. (4 marks)

questions.answer: **Final answer.** Public members are visible everywhere; protected ones in the package and in sub classes; default ones in the package only.
